PullRequest.Title: extensions: wait for installed inventory before installing
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Wait for `queryLocal()` before `workbench.extensions.installExtension` checks for an existing extension.

During startup, the synchronous installed-extension cache can still be empty. A command call with `{ enable: true }` can therefore treat an installed extension as missing and replace it with a Marketplace version. This affects the companion `/ContentMentor` route fix, which needs to preserve an installed pre-release even when the release is older.

The command now loads the installed list before making that decision. Existing option forwarding and the VSIX path are unchanged; no timer or whole-workbench startup wait is added.

## Tests

- All **221 tests** in `extensionsWorkbenchService.test.ts` pass, including six new delayed-inventory cases covering newer pre-release, newer/same/older release, disabled pre-release, and missing extension.
- The new cases execute the registered command and real workbench service, checking install count, version/channel, installation timestamp, enablement, and ordering. They fail against the original command handler.
- Targeted ESLint and TypeScript checks pass. The isolated type check includes Node test-runner declarations.
- The commit's hygiene hook passes.

Test command:

```sh
VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/test/electron-browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.test.ts
```

## Integration notes

The companion route change is microsoft/vscode-dev#1499. It supplies `{ enable: true }` when bootstrapping Content Mentor. Both pieces are needed to reliably preserve installed versions during startup.

Browser verification remains pending: with a newer Content Mentor pre-release installed, visit or refresh `/ContentMentor` and its deep links, and verify the installed version/channel and timestamp are not replaced by the route. Also verify first-time installation and enablement of an existing disabled copy.

No live Marketplace installation or browser end-to-end run was performed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed command path, `queryLocal` implementation, initialization path, and `getInstalled` IPC/filesystem implementation are directly traced. The exact duration varies with server latency, cache state, and extension count, but the added sequential boundary calls and collection-wide work are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Sequential extension-management IPC calls, extension inventory serialization, filesystem/cache scans, and per-extension object remapping.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of configured extension servers (up to local, remote, and web, queried serially) and the installed extension inventory returned by each server; it is paid once per command invocation even after initialization.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased command latency and delayed route/feature startup before installation or enablement can proceed.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The command synchronously searched the already-populated in-memory `local` array and immediately proceeded to install/enable; it issued no inventory IPC or filesystem scan on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every string-based invocation of `workbench.extensions.installExtension` now refreshes all configured extension servers before deciding whether to install or enable one extension.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 500 replaces an in-memory `extensionsWorkbenchService.local.find(...)` with `await extensionsWorkbenchService.queryLocal()` before the same lookup.
Findings.Title: Reuse the initial inventory instead of rescanning every server
Findings.Impact: Invoking the install command— including URI-driven, chat recommendation, and terminal speech installs—blocks before installation/progress on full installed-extension inventory work. In remote or multi-server windows this adds sequential IPC/remote latency; for already-installed extensions, the scan is the entire cost where the old path was an immediate memory lookup.
Findings.Evidence: `ExtensionsWorkbenchService.queryLocal` calls `queryInstalled` sequentially for local, remote, and web servers; `queryInstalled` unconditionally calls `fetchInstalledExtensions`, which invokes `getExtensionsControlManifest` and `getInstalled`. The IPC client sends `getInstalled` across its channel, and the native implementation runs `scanAllExtensions`, resolving extension collections and mapping every installed extension. The service constructor already starts `initialize() -> queryLocal()`, while the added tests intentionally invoke this command before that inventory completes, so the new call can also duplicate the startup request instead of awaiting the existing `whenInitialized` promise.
Findings.Recommendation: Wait for the service's existing initialization/inventory promise and then search `local` (or expose/coalesce a dedicated initial-inventory promise), rather than calling the refresh-oriented `queryLocal()` on every command invocation. This preserves the startup correctness requirement without rescanning warm inventories or duplicating the constructor's in-flight query.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the string-based install command during startup before the installed inventory has loaded.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command cannot decide whether to preserve, install, or enable the requested extension until the added `queryLocal()` completes. Waiting for the existing initial-inventory promise is required for correctness, but starting another refresh is not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and serialize the complete installed-extension inventory, backed by extension profile/directory scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `getInstalled` IPC plus one control-manifest request per configured server; commonly one or two servers, up to local/remote/web. Returned work scales with all installed extensions on each server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command read `extensionsWorkbenchService.local` synchronously and made no inventory boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All requests must finish before the command's in-memory lookup and any install/enable operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve from the gallery and install the requested extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially one gallery/install network workflow for a missing or extension-kind-disabled target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gallery/install work could begin immediately after the in-memory lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing install workflow starts only after the newly added inventory refresh completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured extension-management servers and total installed extensions; effective cardinality is one complete inventory request per server per command, not per extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configured local, remote, and web servers are queried serially by `queryLocal`; within a native server, system and user scans run in parallel and identical in-flight scans are coalesced by the scanner.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workbench service already starts `initialize() -> queryLocal()` at construction. Native scans coalesce identical in-flight scans per server, but the added command still issues another IPC request and repeats response transformation/object mapping/events. After initialization, `queryLocal()` always refreshes again; frontend `local` is cached but bypassed by the changed line. Control manifests have a five-minute server-side cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff adds the await, and the unconditional sequential refresh and IPC/filesystem call chain are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on extension count, scanner cache state, process topology, and remote latency; command frequency is generally user/route driven rather than a render-loop frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: it correctly waits for inventory but starts refresh-oriented work instead of reusing the constructor's in-flight initialization, adding duplicate boundary traffic/work and serial server fan-out on the command critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the command after initialization from URI handling, chat recommendations, terminal speech setup, or another command caller.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The entire inventory refresh completes before checking one ID. For an already installed/enabled target, this refresh is the dominant command cost; for a missing target it delays the existing gallery/install path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-enumerate all installed extensions to answer a single-extension existence check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete installed-inventory IPC per configured server for each command invocation, with O(total installed extensions) returned data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An O(installed extensions) in-memory `find` over the cached workbench inventory, with no IPC or scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks lookup and all subsequent install/enable behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch/install the target extension where required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when the target is already installed and enabled; otherwise the pre-existing single target gallery/install workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged boundary count, but without the preceding refresh latency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When present, starts after the new refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured server count and installed-extension count after server-level grouping; one request serves each complete server inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Server refreshes are serialized local then remote then web; each native server can scan system and user inventories concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Even with a warm in-memory `local` inventory and completed `whenInitialized`, `queryLocal()` unconditionally calls `queryInstalled` for every server. Backend scanner caches may reduce file reads, but IPC, full result serialization/transformation, and collection remapping remain, and completed scan promises are not retained for reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: no warm-cache guard exists in `queryLocal`, and the previous code directly consumed `local`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Warm scanner caches can make local scans cheaper, while remote extension hosts and large inventories make the serialized server chain more expensive. Frequency depends on URI, chat, terminal voice, and external command invocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: every warm invocation gains collection-wide sequential boundary work that was absent before, including no-op requests for already-installed extensions.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The VSIX install proceeds directly to the existing install operation without the added inventory await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing VSIX installation workflow per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing install remains the critical path.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged from the existing VSIX installation implementation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not applicable to the changed branch; URI/VSIX arguments bypass the string-ID lookup and retain existing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line is only inside `typeof arg === 'string'`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to the diff because this branch is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on this scenario; the changed inventory refresh is not reached.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Found one introduced command-latency regression: a single-ID lookup now performs sequential full-inventory refreshes across extension servers instead of reusing the existing initialization/in-memory inventory. Test additions have no production runtime cost.
